### About Lumilens

![Lumilens logo](https://seedtable.com/api/logo/own/2eac3237978122ca97cdb33fb283a850.png)

[Lumilens](https://seedtable.com/companies/lumilens)

United States[Semiconductor](https://seedtable.com/best-semiconductors-startups)146 employeesFounded 2024700.0M USD total raised [Website](https://lumilens.com/)

Lumilens is a photonics company that builds optical interconnects for AI data centres, replacing the copper links between processors with light. Founded in 2024 and based in Belmont, California, it makes 800G and 1.6T pluggable transceivers for scale-out networks, alongside near-package and co-packaged optics for scale-up connections. It emerged from stealth in August 2026 with a Series C of more than $700 million at a $5.5 billion valuation, and says its first product is already shipping to a hyperscaler.

### About This Round

[Lumilens](https://seedtable.com/companies/lumilens), a San Jose-based optical interconnect company, came out of stealth on 6 August 2026 with more than $700 million in Series C funding at a $5.51 billion valuation. The round was co-led by [Atreides Management](https://seedtable.com/companies/atreides-management), [Bain Capital Ventures](https://seedtable.com/companies/bain-capital-ventures), [Meritech](https://seedtable.com/investors/meritech), [Seligman Ventures](https://seedtable.com/investors/seligman-ventures) and [Spark Capital](https://seedtable.com/companies/spark-capital), with [Addition](https://seedtable.com/investors/addition), [Alkeon Capital Management](https://seedtable.com/companies/alkeon-capital-management), [EDBI](https://seedtable.com/companies/edbi), [HarbourVest Partners](https://seedtable.com/companies/harbourvest-partners), [Lingotto](https://seedtable.com/investors/lingotto), Mayfield, [MVP Ventures](https://seedtable.com/companies/mvp-ventures), [Peak XV Partners](https://seedtable.com/companies/peak-xv-partners), [Qualcomm Ventures](https://seedtable.com/companies/qualcomm-ventures), [Redpoint Ventures](https://seedtable.com/companies/redpoint-ventures) and [Thomvest Ventures](https://seedtable.com/companies/thomvest-ventures) also taking part. It brings the total raised to over $900 million.[1](https://www.finsmes.com/2026/08/lumilens-raises-over-700m-in-series-c-funding.html)

The product is LumiCore, a stack that runs from silicon photonics and mixed-signal integrated circuits through electrical-optical interposers to finished optical systems. The vertical span is the point. It lets the company ship near-package optics, co-packaged optics and pluggable transceivers off one technology base, covering both the scale-up fabric inside an AI rack and the scale-out network between racks, rather than picking one packaging bet and living with it.[1](https://www.finsmes.com/2026/08/lumilens-raises-over-700m-in-series-c-funding.html)

The money goes into silicon, systems, software, process engineering and high-volume manufacturing, under CEO Ankur Singla and CTO Ted Schmidt. The constraint it addresses is well understood inside hyperscale data centres: as accelerator counts climb, electrical interconnect runs out of reach and power budget before the compute runs out of headroom, which forces the optics closer to the package.[1](https://www.finsmes.com/2026/08/lumilens-raises-over-700m-in-series-c-funding.html)[2](https://thenextweb.com/news/lumilens-700m-stealth-5-51bn-ai-optical-interconnect)

Five co-leads and a $5.51 billion mark on a company with no public track record is not an ordinary venture structure. It reads closer to a syndicated infrastructure placement, and the register of names says the same thing: [Qualcomm Ventures](https://seedtable.com/companies/qualcomm-ventures), [EDBI](https://seedtable.com/companies/edbi), [HarbourVest Partners](https://seedtable.com/companies/harbourvest-partners), J.P. Morgan Private Capital and [Lingotto](https://seedtable.com/investors/lingotto) are strategic and institutional money rather than early-stage risk capital. That implies the buyers are underwriting a supply-chain position, not a technology thesis. It also relocates the risk. The historical failure mode in co-packaged optics has been yield and packaging at volume rather than the physics, and "high-volume manufacturing operations" is carrying quiet weight in that use-of-funds list. At this valuation Lumilens has to execute like a component supplier, not a startup.

[Read the announcement](https://www.finsmes.com/2026/08/lumilens-raises-over-700m-in-series-c-funding.html)
